artists.biography:
Slowdive are an English shoegaze band that formed in 1989. The band formed in Reading, Berkshire and primarily consisted of Nick Chaplin (bass), Rachel Goswell (vocals, guitar), Neil Halstead (vocals, guitar), and Christian Savill (guitar). Several drummers played with the band, including Ian McCutcheon, Adrian Sell, and most notably Simon Scott who drummed on the first and second albums. Halstead was the band's primary songwriter.

Goswell and Halstead had known each other since early childhood in Reading, Berkshire. Scott left in 1994 and when Savill and Chaplin left the band after the release of Pygmalion, the remaining members renamed the band Mojave 3. The band reunited in 2014.

perplexity.description:
Released in 1995 on Creation Records, Pygmalion is the third and final studio album by English rock band Slowdive before their initial disbandment. Markedly different from their earlier shoegaze works Just for a Day and Souvlaki, Pygmalion embraces a more experimental and minimalist approach, blending ambient textures with electronic elements. The album features sparse, atmospheric arrangements, subdued rhythms, and ethereal soundscapes, reflecting a departure from traditional song structures toward a more introspective and ambient style. This shift was largely driven by Neil Halstead, who dominated the recording process, with only minor contributions from other band members.

Pygmalion stands as a pivotal moment in Slowdive’s discography, marking both the culmination of their original run and a bold stylistic evolution. While it was not a commercial success upon release—peaking at number 108 on the UK Albums Chart—the album received more favorable critical reception than its predecessors, with many later recognizing it as a pioneering work in the ambient and electronic rock genres. Its influence has grown over time, cementing Pygmalion as a cult classic and a significant chapter in the band’s legacy.
